risk_if_not_implemented: Without Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Unauthorized Change Detection, automated control assurance results may be manipulated, misattributed or lose integrity, causing misplaced confidence in control effectiveness. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity (R-SA-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14).

compensating_control_1.name: File Integrity Monitoring (FIM)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a File Integrity Monitor (FIM), or similar change-detection technology, on critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to generate alerts for unauthorized modifications.
compensating_control_1.justification: File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) (MON-27) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Unauthorized Change Detection (CFG-24) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Post Configuration Change Reviews
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to perform after-the-fact reviews of configuration change logs to discover any unauthorized changes.
compensating_control_2.justification: Post Configuration Change Reviews (CHG-11) provides periodic assessment and verification that compensates for the absence of Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Unauthorized Change Detection (CFG-24) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
